short: France agreed to finance the Swedish army in Germany, sustaining their war effort.
full:
Signed on 23 January 1631 between France and Sweden, the Treaty of Bärwalde provided Gustavus Adolphus with an annual French subsidy of 400,000 thalers. In exchange, Sweden committed to maintaining an army of 36,000 men in Germany to counter the Habsburgs, while promising to respect Catholic worship in conquered territories.

The agreement resolved Sweden's pressing financial difficulties and aligned them with Cardinal Richelieu's anti-Habsburg strategy. The influx of French money transformed the Swedish army into a formidable, sustained continental force, enabling the massive campaigns that culminated in their sweeping victories across Germany over the next two years.
